newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The two-year plan by the States to reduce stamp duty on share transactions has failed to boost Australia's role as a share trading centre, with Dr Vince FitzGerald, an executive director with the Allen Consulting Group, saying the country has fallen noticeably behind Singapore and Hong Kong in terms of equity trading. Page 1.

With a report by investment bank Schroders showing foreign banks and insurance companies could buy Australian banks at low prices because of the Federal Government's ban preventing big banks from bidding for each other, investment bankers are trying to persuade major European banks and insurance companies to buy any one of the country's four big banks. Page 1.

Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd's decision on the weekend to let the A$342 million Sydney Casino deal lapse has cost it paper profits of up to A$33 million. The decision came after the company ran into difficulties with the New South Wales government's casino regulator, the New South Wales Casino Control Authority. Page 21.

Following an order from Federal Treasurer Peter Costello to unwind its 76 per cent economic interest in the Ten Group Ltd back to its original 57.5 per cent, Canadian broadcaster CanWest is seeking further meetings with the Government to avoid the ruling and to seek protection of its remaining stake. Page 21.

Speaking on Saturday at a media tour of the A$1.85 billion Crown Casino, which officially opens on Thursday, Crown executive chairman Lloyd Williams said he wants to pursue formal links between the Melbourne and Sydney casinos, but said any equity deals could not evolve in the short term because of the need for legislative approval from the Victorian and New South Wales Governments. Page 21.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (Australia) chief executive John Barnes said yesterday the Deutsche Bank Group's successful A$240 million bid for Axiom Funds Management was hinged on the support of Axiom staff as well as its superior reputation as a funds manager. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd chairman Dick Warburton said yesterday his board was not shocked when Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting announced on Saturday it was opting out of the A$342 million casino management agreement to focus on "key strategic initiatives". Warburton said SHC would seek to build on its relationship with PBL to develop business links with the media group. Page 17.

Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane's debut this week in front of the House of Representatives Standing Committee on Financial Institutions and Public Administration comes amid consternation over monetary policy and rumours that high real interest rates are keeping a lid on small business investment. Page 17.

Following the announcement last week of BHP Steel's radical restructure, including the closure of the Newcastle plant, BHP New Zealand Steel managing director Malcolm Burns said the Glenbrook steelworks, south of Auckland, is fearing for its future after thre difficult months this year. Page 19.

Australian Gold Fields NL, which acquired the flooded Bannockburn mine in Western Australia almost two years ago, defied industry sceptics on its first anniversary on the Australian Stock Exchange last week by announcing the acquisition of a new gold mine in Papua New Guinea that will boost its gold production to 100,000 ounces. Page 21.

Perth-based explorer Anglo Australian Resources is speeding up exploration in north-eastern Tasmania after gold values averaging 2.54 grams a tonne over 24 metres were discovered at Denison East, an almost forgotten mine area about 150 kilometres north-eat of Launceston. Page 21.

Speaking at a mining conference in Toronto recently, Perth-based gold analyst turned mining executive David Russell predicted Fiji was likely to become the next regional target for Australian and Canadian mining firms. Russell, the chief executive officer at the Hyperion Resources Corp, said Fiji had the potential for gold deposits similar to those on Lihir Island in Papua New Guinea. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Potential buyers of Sydney Harbour Casino's management contract, which reportedly include the Victorian racing group TABCorp, AWA and Crown, will have to pay a premium to the offer of A$342 million made previously by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting following a strong share price performance by the gambling group since January. Page 37.

In a move which signals a tougher fees regime for all users of the Australian Stock Exchange as it demutualises, brokers, listed companies and investors face higher charges as part of plans by the exchange to make profits from its CHESS trading system. Page 37.

First Pacific Stockbrokers brewing analyst Tony Young says in a report issued last week that Carlton and United Breweries' strong earnings growth is expected to be downgraded in 1998 and 1999 due to a fall in margins caused by increasing discounting in Australia's beer market and a growing market for discount or "value" brands. Page 37.

- - Last week's decision by BHP to close its Newcastle steelworks in 1999 has ensured that TNT chief executive David Mortimer's inquiry into Government assistance to industry will receive close scrutiny when he hands it to Federal Industry Minister John Moore next month. Page 37.

In a deal which sees the Federal Government deliver its commitment to initial diversity of ownership among the airports, Airport Group Australia, led by United States investors Lockheed Martin and Soros Capital, is set to round out the Coalition's first round of airport privatisations by paying A$600 million-plus for Perth Airport. Page 39.

In comments which come as the ACTU prepares to meet steel group unions in Sydney tomorrow to consider plans to mount a broader campaign than its 24-hour strike by steelworkers at Newcastle, BHP Steel chief Ron McNeilly conceded yesterday the company faced a huge task in communicating its restructure program to its workforce. Page 39.
THE AGE

The Australian Stock Exchange will demutualise and become a profit-making organisation through plans to utilise fully its CHESS trading system. Through a tougher fees regime, broking houses, listed companies and investors will face higher charges, but AS memberships and shares will become more valuable if CHESS demonstrates a profit. Page B1.

Airport Group Australia, led by US investors Lockheed Martin and Soros Capital are likely to win the bid for Perth Airport with a price of over $A500 million. The Federal Government's total return for the sale of the Melbourne, Brisbane and Perth airport will be well over the $A3 billion mark. Page B3.

The giant South African Minorco company has joined the Australian market for the first time in 20 years by linking with Goldstream Mining NL. Goldstream is likely to be well rewarded with the partnership, benefiting from Minorco's mix of exploration properties and expertise. Page B3.

The suspended Minerals Mining and Metallurgy has been re-launched in an alliance between Alistair Cowden, Guido Staltari, and Robert Champion de Crespigny's Normandy group. MMM's assets comprise cash of A$1.2 million, two exploration licences, three houses and various plant and equipment. Page B3.

Following a strong share price performance by Sydney Harbour Casino, potential buyers of the management contract will have to pay a premium to the original offer of A$240 million, made by Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd. Following PBL's withdrawal, it is believed a small group of domestic groups, including the Victorian racing group TAB, AWA and Crown, have shown interest in the contract. Page B3.

Carlton and United Breweries is expected to be hit by a fall in margins due to increased discounting in Australia's beer market over the next two years. Stockbroking analyst Tony Young believes CUB's success will make it more vulnerable to discounting than rival Lion Nathan. Page B6.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
